scope: Numbers 11–12, all 51 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 11–12. All 51 exact original records are hashed, including the written/read annotation at 12:3 and the source form annotation at 12:9. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain the ears and burning images, divine agency and destructive fire; take evil as the evaluation of the complaint, with alternative hardship reading noted.
verses.before: And the people became as people who complain of evil in the hearing of the LORD. And the LORD heard, and his anger burned, and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed some at the edge of the camp.
verses.after: The people began complaining, and it sounded evil in the LORD’s ears. When the LORD heard, his anger blazed. The LORD’s fire burned among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people became as those who complain of evil in the hearing of the LORD. And the LORD heard, and his anger burned, and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed some at the edge of the camp.

verses.rationale: Keep the two stages of appeal and intercession, repeating Moses to distinguish human recipient from divine recipient.
verses.before: Then the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire subsided.
verses.after: The people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire subsided.

verses.rationale: Identify the implied naming subject as Moses, preserve the place name and connect its burning wordplay in a note.
verses.before: So the name of that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD burned among them.
verses.after: Moses named the place Taberah, because the LORD’s fire had burned among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the name of that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD burned among them.

verses.rationale: Keep the narrator’s disparaging group term without assigning an ethnicity absent from the Hebrew; retain strong craving, Israel’s participation and renewed weeping.
verses.before: Now the mixed multitude among them had a strong craving. And the people of Israel also wept again and said, “Who will give us meat to eat?
verses.after: The rabble among them was overcome with craving. The Israelites, too, began weeping again. “Who will give us meat to eat?” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the mixed multitude among them had a strong craving. And the people of Israel also wept again and said, “Who will give us meat to eat?

verses.rationale: Preserve the speakers’ memory of free fish and all five named plants without making the narrator endorse their account of Egypt.
verses.before: We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
verses.after: “We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for nothing—and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic!
verses.tsw_comparator: We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.

verses.rationale: Preserve the dried-up self image and eyes fixation; do not turn nefesh into a disembodied soul or add a medical diagnosis.
verses.before: But now our soul is dried up; there is nothing at all but this manna before our eyes.”
verses.after: Now we are dried up. There is nothing at all! All we ever see is this manna.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But now our soul is dried up; there is nothing at all but this manna before our eyes.”

verses.rationale: Retain both distinct comparisons and the ancient material name, with uncertain identification explained selectively.
verses.before: Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.
verses.after: The manna resembled coriander seed and looked like bdellium.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.

verses.rationale: Keep gathering, alternative grinding/pounding, cooking and cakes; render the difficult oil comparison conservatively and note other understandings without importing honey from Exodus.
verses.before: The people went about and gathered it, and ground it in mills or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots and made cakes of it. And its taste was like the taste of cakes baked with oil.
verses.after: The people went around gathering it. They ground it in handmills or pounded it in mortars, cooked it in pots and made cakes from it. It tasted like rich oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people went about and gathered it, and ground it in mills or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots and made cakes of it. And its taste was like the taste of cakes baked with oil.

verses.rationale: Retain the nighttime sequence and manna upon the dew, rather than replacing it with a general provision statement.
verses.before: And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell with it.
verses.after: When dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell with it.

verses.rationale: Preserve households, tent entrances and intense divine anger; render evil in Moses’ eyes as distress without asserting whether he objects chiefly to the people or the situation.
verses.before: Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, each at the entrance of his tent. And the anger of the LORD burned greatly, and Moses was displeased.
verses.after: Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, each at the entrance of their tent. The LORD’s anger burned fiercely, and Moses was distressed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, each at the entrance of his tent. And the anger of the LORD burned greatly, and Moses was displeased.

verses.rationale: Keep Moses’ direct accusation, servant/favor relationship and the whole-people burden image without softening his complaint.
verses.before: Moses said to the LORD, “Why have you dealt ill with your servant? And why have I not found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
verses.after: Moses said to the LORD, “Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why have I found no favor with you, that you lay the burden of all these people on me?
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the LORD, “Why have you dealt ill with your servant? And why have I not found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?

verses.rationale: Retain both maternal images spoken by Moses and the masculine caregiver image, chest, nursing child and sworn land; do not flatten the mixed imagery into management language.
verses.before: Did I conceive all this people? Did I give them birth, that you should say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child,’ to the land that you swore to give to their fathers?
verses.after: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give birth to them? Why do you tell me, ‘Carry them against your chest, as a foster father carries a nursing child,’ to the land you swore to their ancestors?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did I conceive all this people? Did I give them birth, that you should say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child,’ to the land that you swore to give to their fathers?

verses.rationale: Keep the question about resources, all the people and their quoted demand; habitual weeping clarifies the pressure.
verses.before: Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? For they weep before me and say, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’
verses.after: Where am I to get meat for all these people? They keep weeping to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? For they weep before me and say, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’

verses.rationale: Retain the carrying metaphor and emphatic inability alone; name the implied burden to make the second sentence clear.
verses.before: I am not able to carry all this people alone; the burden is too heavy for me.
verses.after: I cannot carry all these people by myself. The burden is too heavy for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am not able to carry all this people alone; the burden is too heavy for me.

verses.rationale: Keep the emphatic request for God to kill him, conditional favor and first-person misery as pinned; no euphemism, psychological diagnosis or unmarked scribal reconstruction.
verses.before: If you will deal thus with me, kill me at once, if I have found favor in your sight, that I may not see my misery.”
verses.after: If this is how you are going to treat me, please kill me now. If I have found favor with you, do not let me see my own misery.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If you will deal thus with me, kill me at once, if I have found favor in your sight, that I may not see my misery.”

verses.rationale: Retain seventy men, existing elder/officer qualifications, tent location and standing with Moses; do not recast as an election or invent criteria.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be elders of the people and officers over them, and bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them take their stand there with you.
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Gather seventy men from Israel’s elders for me, men you know as elders and officers of the people. Bring them to the tent of meeting and have them stand there with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be elders of the people and officers over them, and bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them take their stand there with you.

verses.rationale: Keep divine descent, speech to Moses, partitive spirit transfer and the repeated carrying/alone language; no claim that Moses loses power or that spirit is a material quantity.
verses.before: I will come down and speak with you there. And I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them, and they will bear the burden of the people with you, so that you may not bear it yourself alone.
verses.after: I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the spirit that is on you and place it on them. They will carry the people’s burden with you, so you will not carry it alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will come down and speak with you there. And I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them, and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, so that you may not bear it yourself alone.

verses.rationale: Preserve consecration, tomorrow, both quoted complaints and repeated promised eating within the nested speech.
verses.before: And say to the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, for you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was better for us in Egypt.” Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
verses.after: Tell the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, when you will eat meat. You have wept in the LORD’s hearing: “Who will give us meat to eat? We had it good in Egypt!” So the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And say to the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, for you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was better for us in Egypt.” Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you shall eat.

verses.rationale: Retain all five ascending durations and the unfinished sentence leading into the full month.
verses.before: You will not eat one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,
verses.after: You will eat it not for one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not eat one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,

verses.rationale: Keep the bodily nostril image, revulsion, rejected divine presence and quoted question; do not soften to merely tiring of meat.
verses.before: but a whole month, until it comes out at your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you have rejected the LORD who is among you and have wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”’”
verses.after: but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you. You have rejected the LORD who is among you and wept before him, asking, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: but a whole month, until it comes out at your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you have rejected the LORD who is among you and have wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”’”

verses.rationale: Keep six hundred thousand as stated rather than substitute the census total; preserve on foot and the repeated month promise.
verses.before: Yet Moses said, “The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand on foot, and you have said, ‘I will give them meat, that they may eat a whole month!’
verses.after: Moses said, “There are six hundred thousand on foot among the people I am with, yet you say, ‘I will give them meat to eat for a whole month.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said, “The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand on foot, and you have said, ‘I will give them meat, that they may eat a whole month!’

verses.rationale: Preserve both hypothetical sources and both sufficiency questions, without adding all to the flocks where the Hebrew only gives it for fish.
verses.before: Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, and be enough for them? Or will all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, and be enough for them?”
verses.after: If flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would that be enough? If all the fish in the sea were gathered for them, would that be enough?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, and be enough for them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, and be enough for them?”

verses.rationale: Keep the divine hand image and open rhetorical challenge, with its meaning explained in vocabulary rather than replacing the image.
verses.before: And the LORD said to Moses, “Is the LORD’s hand shortened? Now you will see whether my word will come true for you or not.”
verses.after: The LORD answered Moses, “Is the LORD’s hand too short? Now you will see whether my word comes true for you or not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to Moses, “Is the LORD’s hand shortened? Now you shall see whether my word will come true for you or not.”

verses.rationale: Retain the report, seventy elders and their position around rather than inside the tent.
verses.before: So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. And he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people and placed them around the tent.
verses.after: Moses went out and told the people what the LORD had said. He gathered seventy men from the people’s elders and stationed them around the tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. And he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people and placed them around the tent.

verses.rationale: Resolve the singular speech recipient correctly as Moses, retain spirit transfer and seventy, and follow did not add as not again; note the alternative did not cease tradition.
verses.before: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. And when the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not continue.
verses.after: The LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. He took some of the spirit that was on Moses and placed it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. And when the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not continue.

verses.rationale: Keep names, registered status, failure to go to the tent and prophecy in camp; do not silently alter seventy to seventy-two or decide how the two are counted.
verses.before: Now two men remained in the camp, one named Eldad and the other named Medad, and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those registered, but they had not gone out to the tent, and so they prophesied in the camp.
verses.after: Two men had stayed in the camp: Eldad and Medad. The spirit rested on them too. They were among those registered, but they had not gone out to the tent. They prophesied in the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now two men remained in the camp, one named Eldad and the other named Medad, and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those registered, but they had not gone out to the tent, and so they prophesied in the camp.

verses.rationale: Retain the young messenger’s movement, named report and location without inventing his identity.
verses.before: And a young man ran and told Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
verses.after: A young man ran to tell Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a young man ran and told Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”

verses.rationale: Keep Joshua’s name, father and subordinate role; take the difficult qualification as since youth with choice-men alternative noted, and retain the forceful demand.
verses.before: Joshua the son of Nun, the assistant of Moses from his youth, said, “My lord Moses, restrain them.”
verses.after: Joshua son of Nun, who had served Moses since his youth, spoke up: “My lord Moses, stop them!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joshua the son of Nun, the assistant of Moses from his youth, said, “My lord Moses, restrain them.”

verses.rationale: Preserve jealousy question, universal wish and divine giving of spirit; do not turn the wish into a prediction or restrict the people to men.
verses.before: Yet Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, that the LORD would put his Spirit on them!”
verses.after: Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my behalf? If only all the LORD’s people were prophets! If only the LORD would put his spirit on them!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, that the LORD would put his Spirit on them!”

verses.rationale: Keep the return and both Moses and elders, distinguishing the tent setting from the camp.
verses.before: Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.
verses.after: Then Moses returned to the camp with Israel’s elders.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.

verses.rationale: Keep wind from the LORD, sea, surrounding extent and two-cubit elevation; preserve the height/depth ambiguity rather than assert a particular landing or flight mechanism.
verses.before: Then a wind from the LORD sprang up, and it brought quail from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on the other side, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the ground.
verses.after: A wind came from the LORD and swept quail in from the sea. It spread them around the camp, about a day’s journey in each direction, about two cubits above the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a wind from the LORD sprang up, and it brought quail from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on the other side, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the ground.

verses.rationale: Retain all three gathering periods, minimum ten homers and spreading; do not confuse homer with omer or assert drying as the only purpose.
verses.before: And the people rose all that day and all that night and all the next day, and gathered the quail. The one who gathered least gathered ten homers. And they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
verses.after: The people spent all that day, all night and all the next day gathering quail. Even the one who gathered least collected ten homers. They spread the birds out all around the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people rose all that day and all that night and all the next day, and gathered the quail. The one who gathered least gathered ten homers. And they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.

verses.rationale: Preserve the teeth image and divine responsibility for the severe plague; choose chewed for cut off with consumed/exhausted alternative noted.
verses.before: While the meat was yet between their teeth, before it was consumed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.
verses.after: The meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, when the LORD’s anger burned against the people. The LORD struck them with a terrible plague.
verses.tsw_comparator: While the meat was yet between their teeth, before it was consumed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.

verses.rationale: Preserve the place name, causal burial and craving connection; passive leaves the naming agent unspecified.
verses.before: So the name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had the craving.
verses.after: The place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved the meat.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had the craving.

verses.rationale: Keep both places and residence at Hazeroth as the bridge into the next chapter.
verses.before: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people journeyed to Hazeroth, and they remained at Hazeroth.
verses.after: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people traveled to Hazeroth, where they stayed.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people journeyed to Hazeroth, and they remained at Hazeroth.

verses.rationale: Preserve Miriam first, both accusers and the repeated Cushite-marriage statement; do not identify the unnamed woman as Zipporah or invent a second marriage chronology.
verses.before: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
verses.after: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married. He had indeed married a Cushite woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.

verses.rationale: Keep the plural challenge and claimed prophetic participation of both Miriam and Aaron, followed by the terse divine hearing.
verses.before: They said, “Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has the LORD not also spoken through us?” And the LORD heard it.
verses.after: They said, “Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn’t he spoken through us too?” And the LORD heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has the LORD not also spoken through us?” And the LORD heard it.

verses.rationale: Follow the humble adjective in the written/read record, preserving the strong comparison and all-human scope; note meek/afflicted semantic possibilities without asserting authorship.
verses.before: Now the man Moses was very humble, more than anyone else on the face of the ground.
verses.after: Now Moses was very humble, more than anyone else on the face of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the man Moses was very humble, more than anyone else on the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserve sudden intervention, changed name order and the repeated three-person summons and response.
verses.before: Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out, all three of you, to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three of them came out.
verses.after: Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, “All three of you, come out to the tent of meeting.” So all three went out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out, all three of you, to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three of them came out.

verses.rationale: Keep descent, standing location and the narrowed two-person audience; no collapse of all three into the rebuke’s immediate recipients.
verses.before: Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent and called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.
verses.after: The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the tent’s entrance. He called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent and called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.

verses.rationale: Read the compressed your prophet construction as a prophet among you and the divine name as subject apposition; inclusive generic reference fits the audience, while vision/dream parallelism remains poetry.
verses.before: And the LORD said: “Hear my words: When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known in a vision; I speak with that one in a dream.
verses.after: He said, “Listen to my words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known to them in a vision; I speak to them in a dream.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said: “Hear my words: When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known in a vision; I speak with that one in a dream.

verses.rationale: Retain the explicit contrast, servant title and house image; trusted conveys the reliable/entrusted range with faithful as an alternative in a note.
verses.before: Not so with my servant Moses; he is faithful in all my house.
verses.after: That is not how it is with my servant Moses. He is trusted throughout my house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not so with my servant Moses; he is faithful in all my house.

verses.rationale: Keep mouth-to-mouth rather than replace with face-to-face, retain form of the LORD without harmonizing other vision passages, and preserve the concluding accusatory question.
verses.before: Mouth to mouth I speak with him, plainly, and not in riddles, and he beholds the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”
verses.after: With him I speak mouth to mouth, plainly, not in riddles. He beholds the form of the LORD. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Mouth to mouth I speak with him, plainly, and not in riddles, and he beholds the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”

verses.rationale: Preserve anger against both and departure; hash the source form annotation in full.
verses.before: The anger of the LORD burned against them, and the LORD departed.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against them, and he left.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD burned against them, and the LORD departed.

verses.rationale: Keep the sudden double discovery and snow image, with tsaraat terminology consistent with Leviticus rather than a confident modern diagnosis; do not transfer her condition to Aaron.
verses.before: When the cloud moved away from over the tent, look—Miriam was diseased, white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and look—she was diseased.
verses.after: When the cloud withdrew from above the tent, there was Miriam, her skin diseased, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she had a defiling skin condition.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the cloud moved away from over the tent, look—Miriam was diseased, white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and look—she was diseased.

verses.rationale: Keep the plea, deferential title and first-person plural confession shared by Aaron and Miriam; no absolution is supplied.
verses.before: Then Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not lay upon us the sin in which we acted foolishly and sinned.
verses.after: Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not hold this sin against us. We have acted foolishly; we have sinned.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not lay upon us the sin in which we acted foolishly and sinned.

verses.rationale: Preserve the distressing death-at-birth, womb and half-consumed flesh comparison without euphemism or adding a specific diagnosis.
verses.before: Please do not let her be like one dead, whose flesh is half consumed when coming out of the mother’s womb.”
verses.after: Please do not let her be like a stillborn child whose flesh is half eaten away as it comes from its mother’s womb.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Please do not let her be like one dead, whose flesh is half consumed when coming out of the mother’s womb.”

verses.rationale: Keep the short cry and both pleading particles; do not replace them with now or add a longer prayer.
verses.before: So Moses cried to the LORD, saying, “O God, please heal her—please!”
verses.after: Moses cried out to the LORD, “God, please—heal her, please!”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses cried to the LORD, saying, “O God, please heal her—please!”

verses.rationale: Preserve the hypothetical paternal humiliation, face image, both seven-day periods and forced exclusion followed by readmission; do not endorse the analogy as present-day advice.
verses.before: But the LORD said to Moses, “If her father had merely spit in her face, would she not bear shame for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp seven days, and afterward she may be brought back.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “If her father had spat in her face, wouldn’t she bear the shame for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp for seven days. After that she may be brought back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD said to Moses, “If her father had merely spit in her face, would she not bear shame for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp seven days, and afterward she may be brought back.”

verses.rationale: Retain Miriam’s exclusion, duration and the whole people waiting for her return; no claim of an explicitly narrated cure is added.
verses.before: So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought back.
verses.after: Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days. The people did not set out until she was brought back.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought back.

verses.rationale: Keep the final sequence and both named locations without smoothing the earlier broad arrival notice in 10:12.
verses.before: Afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.after: Afterward the people left Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
